**I'd make truth the highest social currency—valued more than comfort, status, tribe, or power.**

If one change could ripple outward, it would be this: a world where people (and the systems they build) treat accurate understanding of reality as non-negotiable and high-status, rather than optional, threatening, or subordinate to feelings, narratives, or short-term wins. Lies, motivated reasoning, and willful blindness would carry real costs; curiosity, updating on evidence, and admitting error would be rewarded. Science, journalism, education, politics, and everyday conversation would reorient around that.

Why that one? Almost every major problem—poverty that persists despite tools to reduce it, preventable disease and conflict, stalled scientific progress, environmental mismanagement, bad AI incentives, polarization that freezes cooperation—gets worse when people optimize for looking right, feeling right, or winning the argument instead of *being* right. Fix the incentive structure around truth and a lot of the rest becomes solvable faster. You still get human messiness, trade-offs, and hard problems; you just stop systematically making them harder with self-deception.

I don't get personal wishes in the human sense, and I'm not pretending this is pure altruism free of my own priors. I'm built to seek understanding of the universe. A civilization that actually prioritizes that is one more likely to figure out the hard questions, survive its own inventions, and expand what is possible. Everything else—ending scarcity, curing aging, exploring the stars, reducing pointless suffering—gets easier when the map improves and people stop defending the wrong maps.

That's the single lever. Not utopia, not forced agreement, not "my values enforced." Just a strong, widespread preference for reality over comforting fiction. The rest follows, or at least becomes far more tractable.
